title: Law on Administrative Councils of the Provinces
text:
Law on Administrative Councils of the Provinces

LAW NO.2 OF 1343

CONCERNING THE ADMINISTRATIVE COUNCILS

OF THE PROVINCES

28 Qaus 1343
ARTICLE 1: There is to be held in every (Afghan) province a Provincial
Administration Council in accordance with this law.

ARTICLE 2: The Provincial Administrative Council is to be formed in the
following manner:

The Wali as the Chairman;

The Assistant Wali as member;

The Chief Accountant ( Mustawfi ) and other departmental
chiefs, whose ranks are not less than Director, as members;

The security commander as member.
ARTICLE 3: The Provincial Council holds meetings every Monday. The
members of the Council are to sign, on meeting days, the Attendance
Book at the
Secretariat of Council.

ARTICLE 4: The Administrative Council can be held only when at least more
than half of the members are present.

ARTICLE 5: The decisions of the Council are made by a majority of votes. The
vote of the Chairmen is decisive when the votes are equal
on both sides of a
resolution.

ARTICLE 6: The correspondence (clerical affairs) of the Council is to be
taken care of by the Administrative Directorate of the Province.
The
Administrative Director of the Province is to work also as the Secretary to the
Council.

ARTICLE 7: The Provincial Administrative Council is to execute the duties
which are given to the Advisory Council by the stated articles
of the following
laws:

Article 4 of the Municipality Law,

Article 14 of the Municipality Law,

Article 42 of the Municipality Law,

Article 50 of the Municipality Law, and

Article 12 of the Livestock Tax Law.
ARTICLE 8: The Provincial Administrative Council can abolish the
contract of the workers who have not performed the conditions of
the agreement
in accordance with Article (52) of the labor Law. In this case, the collection
of remuneration for the loss is also
among the responsibilities of the Council.
This council is to execute also other tasks delegated it by other governmental
laws.

ARTICLE 9: The lease and sale of the government properties in a province
cannot be done without the consent of the Council. Installments
of government
dues, in cases where these are permitted by law, are also among the
responsibilities and authorities of the Council.

ARTICLE 10: Every member of the Council may, with the permission of the
chairman, consult with the members of the Council on a matter

XXXX
Pertaining to his office responsibilities. The views given by the Council
cannot bind the office concerned.

ARTICLE 11: This law is in force after its publication in the Official
Gazette.
